David — thanks for the walkthrough last week. Before we lock the MAP and start procurement, procurement has two narrow asks so we can model FY27 spend: 1) a clear per-API-call tokens/$ estimate under your proposed runtime (Redwood-7B-quant), and 2) the gating assumptions for caching and batching that materially change the unit price.

Can you send a short decomposition we can slot into the financial model (tokens per user flow, expected KV cache hit %, batching distribution, expected 95th latency given batching)? If you can include a short sensitivity (±10% cache hit, batch size +/-1) that would be perfect.

We need this by EOD next Tuesday (11/30) to keep the procurement window open.

—Samira
Procurement Manager, NovaMed

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@novamed.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ops-Fin checkpoint: token econ decomposition and close cadence

Samira — thanks, understood. High level first pass below; attaching a concise MAP worksheet and our simulation CSV (attached). Grace and Karthik are looped for technical clarifications.

Summary (single-line): baseline tokens/$ assumes Redwood-7B-quant at $0.0018 per generated token (hosted, after volume tiers) with an expected effective tokens-per-dollar of ~560 tokens/$ under current traffic shape (avg gen 120 tokens/call, 35% KV-hit, batch size 4 median).

Decomposition and assumptions:
- Model variant: Redwood-7B-quant (production tuned).
- Avg input tokens per call (prompt + context): 45 tokens.
- Avg generation per call: 120 tokens (this is P50 for the pilot flows you provided).
- Total tokens per call (billable): 165 tokens.
- Pricing reference: $0.0018 per generated token (hosted listed rate after committed tier).
- Baseline per-call cost (no caching/batching): 165 * $0.0018 = $0.297.

Ops levers and effective unit economics:
1) KV / prefix caching: we estimate a 35% hit rate on prefix/KV cache for NovaMed's call patterns (templates + repeated context). When a cache hit avoids the first NKV tokens (average saved generation tokens = 40), effective billable tokens drop.
   - With 35% hit -> effective tokens/call ~149 -> tokens/$ ~ 547 -> effective cost/call ~$0.268.
2) Batching: runtime batching reduces GPU cycles but billing is still per-token; batching mainly influences latency and throughput needs rather than direct token unit price. However, better batching reduces infra marginal cost and enables a lower committed tier. We model batch size distribution: median 4, P90 8.
3) Prefetch/Prefill: prefetching predictable prompts (e.g., standard triage templates) can push cache hit to ~50% in optimistic scenario.

Sensitivity table (included in attached MAP_v2.xlsx):
- Cache hit +/- 10%: at 25% hit -> cost/call ~$0.281; at 45% hit -> cost/call ~$0.255.
- Median batch +/-1: batch median 3 -> small impact on tail latency (P95 +60ms), negligible on token billing; affects capacity planning.

Operational gating (MAP checklist items):
- Prefetch test (customer-side sample): validate cacheable prompt fraction >= 30% by pilot week 2.
- Throughput test: verify batch median between 3–6 at pilot traffic.
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 800ms for 90% of traffic; if not met, fallback to a smaller model variant for real-time routes.

Action items and timeline:
- 11/27: Redwood to run a 24h prefetch sim (attached prefeth-sim-results.csv).
- 11/29: internal ops-fin sync (David + Grace + Karthik) to finalize MAP economics note.
- 11/30 EOD: deliver final MAP worksheet and signoff for procurement.

Attached: MAP_v2.xlsx (summary + sensitivity), prefetch-sim-results.csv (sim by hour).

If this covers it I can convert to a single-slide summary for procurement. Want me to do that?

Best,
David Kim
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ops-Fin checkpoint: token econ decomposition and close cadence

Looping in a couple of clarifying technical notes to make sure procurement's model uses conservative numbers for capacity planning. Copying the relevant lines you'd want in the MAP worksheet: 

1) Cache hit definition: our 35% is KV/prefix cache hit *at-inference*; it does not include hashed-response cache or long-term embedding cache. For NovaMed's flows (lots of templated triage prompts), 35% is realistic but requires the prompt hygiene we discussed.
2) Saved tokens on hit: I model saved generated tokens = 40 (median). If prompts have long slot expansions, treat saved tokens as +50.
3) Batch sizing: median 4 assumed, but batch variance matters for tail GPU memory. Please include P95 batch size in the worksheet; if P95 > 12 we recommend an autoscale buffer.
4) Quantization fallback: if we must fall back to unquantized model for specific secure flows, unit price increases by ~1.6x — call this out as a contingency.

Also note: token-based cost for embeddings vs. generation differs; if NovaMed routes embedding calls to the same endpoint, split those in the financial model (they are cheaper per token but account for separate throughput).

I'll be available on 11/29 afternoon to review the final numbers.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Procurement reviewed the sensitivity and the MAP worksheet, and we have two quick clarifications before we finalize: 1) can you add the contingency line for quantization fallback as a % uplift in the one-page summary, and 2) can you confirm the expected committed tier threshold (tokens/month) where the $0.0018/generated-token rate applies?

If we get those before EOD Wednesday (12/2) we can greenlight the PO window. Attached is the internal procurement checklist (we referenced your MAP_v2.xlsx).

Next steps we agreed: Redwood to provide a one-slide summary with the contingency uplift and a recommended committed-tier breakpoint; NovaMed procurement will respond with a PO term sheet by 12/7 pending legal.

—Samira
